For the officer joining this caseload, here is a concise orientation note:  

**District Concentration**: Cases are concentrated in **فیصل آباد** (Faisalabad: 19 cases), **لاہور** (Lahore: 18 cases), and **راولپنڈی** (Rawalpindi: 10 cases), with smaller numbers in Islamabad (5), Chiniot (5), Hyderabad (5), Karachi East (5), Karachi Central (5), and Multan (1) [Document 1].  

**Case Mix**: Current cases (2026) include **39 PPC** (up from 13 in 2024), **16 Arms Ordinance 1965** (down from 13 in 2024), and new categories like **CNSA 1997 (12)**, **PECA 2016 (9)**, **Punjab Domestic Violence Act (4)**, and **Illegal Dispossession Act 2005 (2)**. This reflects a diversification of legal issues, with a sharp rise in PPC-related offenses [Document 2].  

**Reporting Delays**: The mean time from incident to report is **1401.3 minutes (~23.4 hours)** in 2026 (across 51 FIRs), significantly slower than **15.0 minutes** in 2024 (across 13 FIRs) [Document 4].  

**Arrest Rates**: Only **11 FIRs** (1 in 6.6) record an arrest, while **62 FIRs** have no arrests. This includes 77 accused entries marked as "under investigation" or "absconding" [Document 3].  

**Weapon Licensing**: **30 cases** involve recovered weapons with **no licence recorded**, and **2 cases** have **no licence status at all** [Document 5].  

**Accused Profile**: **67 male** (مرد) and **24 female** (عورت) accused across 94 total entries, with **3 cases** having unknown gender [Document 6].  

Officers should prioritize districts with higher case volumes, prepare for delayed reporting, and focus on PPC and new legislation-specific offenses. Unlicensed weapons and low arrest rates may require enhanced investigative strategies.
